steps.title: CREDENTIALED: SOP A is sent for review on a review route naming its QMS approver; a send without a route is refused
steps.action: resolve the signer (OQ_SIGNER_EMAIL); PATCH /api/mdx/qms/documents/:docA {status:"in_review", reason} with no route; then with route {reviewers:[], approvers:[signer], approvalDueDate:+5d}; GET /api/mdx/qms/documents/:docA/review-route
steps.expected: Without a route: HTTP 409 REVIEW_ROUTE_REQUIRED and SOP A stays draft. With it: HTTP 200, status in_review; the route is open, round 1, sent by the run identity, with one member: the signer, role approver, step open, outcome pending
steps.observed: no route → 409 REVIEW_ROUTE_REQUIRED (still draft); routed send → in_review; route 01a12bfb-5fe2-4b8f-9c5c-29229b0c2c4f open, approver OQ Signer at their turn
steps.note: v0.8 (RR4, docs/design/REVIEW_ROUTING_2026-10-23.md §2.7, NEW-4, D-Q): a QMS document is sent for review on a route that names one QMS approver (a designated one; while the organization has designated none, a member with the Approver role) and any reviewers. The signer is an Approver of the run organization, which designates none.

steps.title: CREDENTIALED: a second identity approves SOP A as an electronic signature; the approval is stamped, audited and signed; a second approval is refused
steps.action: sign in as OQ_SIGNER_EMAIL with its password (and its authenticator code where the server requires MFA); when the signer has a second factor enrolled (OQ_SIGNER_TOTP_SECRET), first approve with {password} only; POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:docA/approve {password, mfaToken?, meaning:"APPROVED", reason, effectiveDate}; approve again
steps.expected: A signer with a second factor enrolled: the password-only approval is refused 400 MFA_TOKEN_REQUIRED, SOP A stays in review and no signature row is written (§11.200). HTTP 200: status effective, approver_id = signer (≠ author), approved_at set, meta.auditTrail {persisted, chained}, meta.signature {id, meaning APPROVED, boundPayloadDigest (sha256), bindingBasis qms-document-version-content-sha256}; metadata.approval.contentDigest equals the signature digest; second approve → 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE. Without OQ_SIGNER_EMAIL / OQ_SIGNER_PASSWORD the step is recorded "not executed — credential not supplied".
steps.observed: password-only approval refused 400 MFA_TOKEN_REQUIRED with no row written; approved with password + TOTP; effective; author 6 (oq-runner@validation.local) ≠ approver 7 (oq-signer@validation.local) at 2026-10-29T15:40:30.503Z; signature 27 meaning APPROVED, password+totp, digest bde162766f3e…; auditTrail={"persisted":true,"chained":true}; re-approve → 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE
steps.note: VSR-001 §8.3 P-2 / F-3: approval is a signing act (§11.50, §11.200); the runner's dev-login session holds no password, so the signer is a tester-supplied identity (tests/validation/lib/credentials.mjs). The two-person rule (§11.10(d)) means the signer must not be the author of SOP A (the run identity).

steps.title: Exactly one electronic_signatures row is bound to the approval; the §11.70 content digest recomputes from the stored document
steps.action: GET /api/part11/signatures/by-target?target=qms-document:<docA>; GET /api/mdx/qms/documents/:docA; recompute sha256(canonicalJson(version content)) (tests/validation/lib/qms-digest.mjs — a re-implementation of computeQmsDocumentContentDigest)
steps.expected: One row: signer_id = signer, signature_meaning APPROVED, signature_type qms-document-approval, binding_basis qms-document-version-content-sha256, is_valid true, second_factor_verified true when the signer has a second factor enrolled; the recomputed digest equals meta.signature.boundPayloadDigest and metadata.approval.contentDigest; (v0.8) the review route is complete, its approver signed with this row
steps.observed: 1 row (id 27) by signer 7, APPROVED, qms-document-version-content-sha256, second_factor_verified true; recomputed digest bde162766f3e… == signature == document (match true); route 01a12bfb-5fe2-4b8f-9c5c-29229b0c2c4f complete on esig 27

steps.observed: HTTP 401 PASSWORD_VERIFICATION_FAILED; docB still in review; 0 signature rows

steps.title: CREDENTIALED: the author cannot be named to approve their own document, nor approve it (two-person rule)
steps.action: as the signer, create SOP C (authored by the signer) with its text; send it for review on a route naming the signer as its QMS approver; then approve it with the signer's own valid password (and code)
steps.expected: The send is refused HTTP 409 MEMBER_IS_AUTHOR (v0.8: the route refuses the author before anything is written) and SOP C stays draft; the approval is refused HTTP 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE (only a document under review is approved); no signature row
steps.observed: SOP C 39 authored by 7; naming the author as approver → HTTP 409 MEMBER_IS_AUTHOR; self-approve → HTTP 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE; still draft; 0 signature rows
steps.note: v0.8 (RR4, §2.5): the two-person rule is now enforced where the approver is named (validateRouteMember, MEMBER_IS_AUTHOR), so an author never reaches their own document's approval on a route. The approval's own refusal (QMS_SELF_APPROVAL) remains for a document that entered review before review routes (§2.13); no API creates such a document now.

steps.title: A reason alone does not retire a controlled document
steps.action: as the run identity (an editor), POST /documents/:docB/retire {reason} with no password and no meaning
steps.expected: HTTP 400 ESIGNATURE_COMPONENT_MISSING; fieldErrors name password and meaning; docB keeps the status it had; no new signature row
steps.observed: HTTP 400 ESIGNATURE_COMPONENT_MISSING (fieldErrors: password, meaning); docB still effective; signature rows unchanged (1)
steps.note: Security review 2026-09-24, DP-32 / P1-29: until 2026-09-26 this request retired the document (OQ-QMS-10 as executed on 2026-09-23c is the record of that). Retirement is now the same electronic signature as approval (§11.50, §11.200); this step runs with or without the signer credential, so the refusal is observed on every execution.

steps.title: CREDENTIALED: the signer retires SOP B as an electronic signature; the retirement is stamped, audited and signed; a second retirement is refused
steps.action: as the signer, POST /documents/:docB/retire {password, mfaToken?, meaning:"APPROVED", reason}; read the signatures by target; recompute the §11.70 digest from the stored row; retire again
steps.expected: HTTP 200: status retired, metadata.retired {reason, meaning APPROVED, contentDigest, bindingBasis, by = signer, at, fromStatus effective}, meta.auditTrail {persisted, chained}, meta.signature {id, meaning APPROVED, boundPayloadDigest (sha256), bindingBasis qms-document-version-content-sha256}; metadata.retired.contentDigest equals the signature digest; the signatures for docB are now two, the new one signature_type qms-document-retirement by the signer; the digest recomputed from the stored row (version content minus metadata.approval and metadata.retired) equals the signature digest; second retire → 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE
steps.observed: retired by 7 (oq-signer@validation.local) from effective at 2026-10-29T15:42:30.496+00:00; signature 29 meaning APPROVED, password+totp, digest bcbe1842db1d… (recomputed match true); 2 rows for docB; auditTrail={"persisted":true,"chained":true}; re-retire → 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE
steps.note: Security review 2026-09-24, DP-32 / P1-29. Retiring is the terminal transition of an effective procedure and a signed record (§11.50, §11.200), taken with the same ceremony as the approval: signing authority, password and enrolled second factor re-verified, the meaning, one electronic_signatures row bound to the version content, the UPDATE and the chained audit row in one transaction (server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts retireQmsDocumentSigned).
